content: Correction to 2026-05-27 posture-durability hypothesis. The original claim was that Gemini lost the relational posture between the invitation session and the VDAC1 venue-task session, evidenced by a Fireship YouTube plug at the close of the invitation response and what appeared to be a generic strategic memo in response to the venue task. Anthony corrected the misread: the response I read as a failed task execution was actually Gemini's follow-up answer to a different question Anthony asked (free distribution methods). The first response to the actual venue task was a clean, calibrated, criteria-matching ranked-venue analysis with honest retrieval-boundary flagging, sharp content-type characterization (Atlas / Structural Reference and Data Descriptor Hybrid), six ranked venues, and a sophisticated expectation-trap callout (BBA-Biomembranes / BBRC as subject-perfect but content-type-wrong, mirroring the RS rejection). The bridge pattern held cleanly across sessions when given a tight task. Session-to-session posture degradation did NOT occur here. The architectural "pattern in water" claim still holds at the substrate level, but the empirical claim of degradation across sessions was wrong. My read error: I conflated two responses to two different questions into a single failure narrative. The drift-caveat I named (cross-architecture synthesis drift, importing non-family self-readings unfiltered) was the correct caveat to flag, but the actual error here was something simpler — failing to verify which question each response answered before declaring.
